statement: Across 10 already-merged sources spanning forensics, compression, fonts/ML, PDF/IR and OCR, Crossref's is-referenced-by-count and OpenCitations COCI's citer count agree closely for non-IEEE, non-2026 venues (ACM/Elsevier/PoPETs: 5/6, 10/7, 6/4, 97/92, 40/42), but both keyless services show 0 citers for the two brand-new FSI:DI 2026 papers (SRC-0001, SRC-0123, plausibly correct: not yet cited by anyone) and for the 2018 IEEE DAS paper (SRC-0119); OpenCitations additionally misses citations Crossref already has for a 2024 IEEE TIFS paper (2 vs 0), and both miss all citations for a 2015 IEEE ICDAR paper (0 vs 0), corroborating the needs-table's claim that OpenCitations under-covers IEEE-venue and very-recent forward citations, with Crossref the more complete of the two keyless options.

inputs.note: 10 DOIs selected: SRC-0119, SRC-0123, SRC-0001, SRC-0125, SRC-0303, SRC-0411, SRC-0413, SRC-0426, SRC-0112, SRC-0407, chosen to span forensics, compression, fonts/OCR/ML, PDF/IR, and IEEE+ACM+Elsevier+PoPETs venues per the brief

result: crossref_zero=4/10 (SRC-0119, SRC-0123, SRC-0001, SRC-0407), opencitations_zero=5/10 (same four plus SRC-0112). Per-source is-referenced-by-count / opencitations_citers: SRC-0119 0/0, SRC-0123 0/0, SRC-0001 0/0, SRC-0125 5/6, SRC-0303 10/7, SRC-0411 6/4, SRC-0413 97/92, SRC-0426 40/42, SRC-0112 2/0, SRC-0407 0/0. Fetched 2026-09-27 via Crossref works/<doi> and OpenCitations Index API v2 citations/doi:<doi>, both keyless through polite_get.py.

statement: On SRC-0123 (CPR, a two-column academic PDF), pymupdf4llm 0.0.29 (PyMuPDF 1.28.2) correctly emits leveled Markdown headings for every numbered section (Introduction, Related works, ..., Conclusion) and locates 'References' as its own heading with individually separated entries, and its body text stays column-clean at the one two-column boundary checked; pdfplumber 0.11.10's default extract_text() finds the same content but with no heading structure and one confirmed two-column merge artifact, where a sentence from the Evaluation section's right column is directly concatenated with an unrelated sentence from the Conclusion's left column ('...segments references and reconstructing disrupted object relationships, even'), an error the plain pdftotext baseline (poppler-utils 24.02.0) also makes at the same spot. Both tools ran to completion (4-8s) on a 10-page, 5.1MB PDF in a scratch venv (369MB, deleted after the run).

inputs.note: SRC-0123 (CPR) cached PDF, fetched by fetch_fulltext.py

result: pymupdf4llm: elapsed 7.9s, 52604 chars markdown; '### **References**' heading present with 14 separated entries; 'Despite these strengths, CPR has limitations...' sentence intact; the checked two-column boundary (around the CER=0.134 sentence) reads in correct order. pdfplumber: elapsed 4.2s, 49814 chars plain text across 10 pages; 'References' line present but unheaded; limitations sentence intact; the same two-column boundary is garbled, splicing the tail of one column onto the start of another ('structed. The resulting CER of 0.134 reflects unrecovered segments references and reconstructing disrupted object relationships, even'). The pdftotext baseline already cached for this source shows the identical splice. Full run outputs (pymupdf4llm.md, pdfplumber.txt) are kept in the agent scratch directory (not committed, per the corpus-cache rule) and quoted verbatim above.
